title: 2024 capital budget review and infrastructure funding
subtitle: Development charge shortfalls, new debt, reserve funds, road timing, traffic calming and the budget timeline.
overview: The Special Finance and Corporate Services Committee spent the afternoon reviewing the draft 2024 capital budget and ten-year forecast. The minutes record no motions, so the committee made no recommendations. Members heard presentations and asked staff clarifying questions.

Staff said most capital spending goes to renewing existing infrastructure, and that more than half of funding comes from enterprises such as water, sanitary and stormwater. That enterprise share rose by $165 million, largely because of the Water Infrastructure Program update. Development charge revenue has dropped because of provincial changes, an estimated $5.5M loss up to mid-November. Staff said the City may need to issue development charge debt for large growth projects in 2024 and 2025, to be repaid from future charges. Overall City debt has been falling for a decade, and many reserve funds are positive but below target.

Next steps: a public input meeting followed later that day, the Mayor tables the 2024 budget at a Special Council meeting on December 4, 2023, amendments are due to the Clerk by December 11, and a final budget meeting is set for December 14.
debate: Several councillors raised road timing: residents expected some reconstructions sooner, and staff said forecasts beyond the current year are estimates that shift with asset condition, coordination and funding, while maintenance such as pothole repair continues.

On development charge debt, a councillor asked whether growth could stall. Staff said planned projects can proceed using debt, but servicing it narrows funding for future growth projects, and the province's promise to make municipalities whole remains unclear and conditional.

Councillors repeatedly said speeding is the top resident complaint and that traffic calming looked small beside cycling spending. Staff pointed to complete streets design in road reconstructions and agreed to map all related investments for the 2025 budget; members also asked for more discretionary tools and police enforcement.
One councillor urged better planning for eventual replacement of new facilities, not only their construction. Staff said asset management work will improve how money is set aside.
On the Humane Society's expected expansion funding request, staff said it could be met from capital contingencies already in the budget, and the mayor invited councillors' views.
